```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Demand evidence in A is concrete and current. Caregivers describe running medication and doctor records in Google Sheets and group texts. B's demand evidence is one 2020 HN comment and one blog post, and neither points to an unmet need that existing tools fail to meet.",
    "A's price point is supported by several live, small-team competitors charging $4–7/month (SplitKin, CircleCare, CompassCare). Each is sourced with a URL. Paid conversion at that price is plausible for a solo operator within 90 days.",
    "B's own case against undercuts its core thesis. The brief says retrieval and habit, not capture or connection, is the real churn driver. It also says the exact Memex pitch was already tried by a funded team without mainstream traction, and that Tana moved away from pure PKM monetization.",
    "B faces a free, deeply entrenched default in Obsidian, which has a plugin ecosystem. That makes $10–15/month for a new entrant a harder ask than A's sub-$7 price against fragmented apps.",
    "A has a reachable, specifically defined payer: the primary adult-child caregiver. It also has sourced, low-cost community channels. B's channels are only Product Hunt and YouTube sponsorships, and neither shows that conversion to paid will follow."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence rests on a 2020 Hacker News comment about accumulating 7,000 links. It is old and anecdotal. It shows hoarding behavior, not a willingness to pay for a new tool or a gap that Obsidian or Roam leave open. The claim that WorldBrain's Memex 'attracted funding' is weak too: it is sourced only to a GitHub repo, which does not document funding.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both ideas face crowded fields. A has serious risks of its own: a sourced user quote demands the app be free, multi-sibling activation creates friction, customer lifetimes are naturally short, and FTC health-data and Washington MHMDA compliance applies. A wins because its demand and pricing evidence is more specific, more current, and more directly tied to people already paying small teams. B has better per-user price potential but weaker proof that anyone would switch and pay."
}
```
